name: Tesamorelin / MOTS-c
used_for: Marketed by clinics as a body recomposition stack, combining a growth hormone-releasing hormone analog with a mitochondrial peptide for visceral fat reduction and metabolic support.
summary: This blend pairs tesamorelin, an FDA-approved growth hormone-releasing hormone analog (labeled for a specific HIV-related fat condition), with MOTS-c, an unapproved mitochondrial peptide studied mostly in cells and rodents. No approved product contains the combination, and no combination-specific human study was found. A clinic page says the rationale for such stacks rests more on mechanism and limited research than on large human trials. Each component's own page holds the detailed information (Tesamorelin and MOTS-c); formulations and sources vary by seller.

internet_claims.claim: A Miami anti-aging clinic's blog (Rewind Anti-Aging, which sells peptide therapy) describes tesamorelin plus MOTS-c as a body recomposition stack aimed at visceral fat reduction and metabolic optimization, with a protocol lasting several months under lab monitoring.

The same clinic says most of its peptides are investigational or compounded and not FDA-approved for these uses, and that the synergy rationale is grounded more in mechanism and limited research than in large human trials.

dose.summary: No study has tested a combined dose of tesamorelin and MOTS-c. Sellers describe doses only: a pre-mixed three-peptide product with equal small amounts of each, or a protocol that gives each peptide at its own dose.

items.text: RxPepsDirect, a compounded-peptide seller, sells a Lean Stack vial that also contains SS-31, a third peptide, and describes a starting dose of 20 units (0.2 mL) giving 0.4 mg each of SS-31, MOTS-c and tesamorelin per injection.
items.label: internet

items.text: PeptIQ, a peptide guide site with referral links to telehealth partners, describes a stack with tesamorelin at 1 mg daily rising to 2 mg daily after 2 weeks, plus MOTS-c at either 500 mcg to 1 mg daily or 5 mg two to three times a week. The guide also includes retatrutide.
items.label: internet

timing.summary: No study covers timing of the combination. One online guide says the two peptides are injected separately, MOTS-c in the morning and tesamorelin in the evening, and that MOTS-c is added after tesamorelin has been started.

items.text: PeptIQ, a peptide guide site with referral links to telehealth partners, says tesamorelin is injected in the evening before bed and MOTS-c in the morning, as separate injections, and recommends adding MOTS-c 2 to 3 weeks after settling on tesamorelin rather than starting both together.
items.label: internet

frequency.summary: No study covers how often to give the combination. Online sources describe daily tesamorelin with MOTS-c on 3 to 5 days a week, or a pre-mixed product used 5 days on and 2 days off.

items.text: Rewind Anti-Aging, a Miami clinic that sells peptide therapy, says tesamorelin is given as a daily injection under the skin and MOTS-c often 3 to 5 times per week.
items.label: internet

items.text: RxPepsDirect, a compounded-peptide seller, says its three-peptide Lean Stack is injected daily for 5 days with 2 days off.
items.label: internet

cycle_length.summary: No study covers how long to run the combination. Online sources describe 12 to 26 week protocols with lab monitoring, sometimes with breaks, and none is backed by a combination trial.

items.text: Rewind Anti-Aging, a Miami clinic that sells peptide therapy, describes tesamorelin plus MOTS-c as a protocol lasting several months under lab monitoring.
items.label: internet

items.text: Rewind Anti-Aging, a Miami clinic that sells peptide therapy, says protocols generally run 12 to 26 weeks, with metabolic labs at the start, at 8 weeks and periodically after.
items.label: internet

items.text: PeptIQ, a peptide guide site with referral links to telehealth partners, says 12 weeks is a reasonable cycle, followed by a 4-week break from tesamorelin, and that MOTS-c is run in 8 to 12 week cycles with 4-week breaks.
items.label: internet

storage_and_handling.summary: No study covers storage of a mixed product. One compounding seller says its pre-mixed three-peptide vial is refrigerated with a 90-day beyond-use date.

items.text: RxPepsDirect, a compounded-peptide seller, says its Lean Stack (tesamorelin, MOTS-c and SS-31 in one vial) is pre-reconstituted by the pharmacy, needs no bacteriostatic water, is refrigerated and carries a 90 day beyond-use date from compounding.
items.label: internet

mechanism.summary: No source describes how the combination works in people. Clinics argue that the two peptides act on different pathways, but this is reasoning from each peptide, not a combination finding.

items.text: Rewind Anti-Aging, a Miami clinic that sells peptide therapy, says tesamorelin stimulates growth hormone release to promote fat breakdown while MOTS-c supports mitochondrial function and metabolic efficiency through AMPK activation, and markets the pair as a body recomposition stack aimed at visceral fat reduction and metabolic optimization.
items.label: internet

best_documented_effect.summary: No study of tesamorelin with MOTS-c in people was found, and no registry record for the combination turned up. Sources that sell or promote the stack say so themselves.

items.text: Rewind Anti-Aging, a Miami clinic that sells peptide therapy, says most of its peptides are investigational or compounded and not FDA-approved for these uses, and that the synergy rationale is grounded more in mechanism and limited research than in large human trials.
items.label: internet

items.text: Peptide Protocol Wiki, a site that lists peptide sellers, says no published research has tested any two- or three-peptide combination from a stack that includes tesamorelin and MOTS-c with AOD-9604.
items.label: internet

side_effect_groups.title: No combination safety data
side_effect_groups.summary: No study reports side effects of tesamorelin and MOTS-c together. One site notes there is no toxicology data for combinations in a related stack.

items.text: Peptide Protocol Wiki, a site that lists peptide sellers, says there is no toxicology data for any two- or three-peptide combination from a stack of AOD-9604, tesamorelin and MOTS-c.
items.label: internet

side_effect_groups.title: Seller guidance
side_effect_groups.summary: A compounding seller of a three-peptide product tells users to report swelling, joint pain or hand numbness, and lists who should avoid it. This is seller advice, not trial data.

items.text: RxPepsDirect, a compounded-peptide seller, says users of its Lean Stack (tesamorelin, MOTS-c and SS-31) should report new swelling, joint pain or hand numbness to a clinician, and that it is not for people with active cancer, pituitary tumors or pregnancy.
items.label: internet
